note: Every fixture is generated by the named program: it is written for this repository rather than collected, which is what makes the corpus shippable and re-runnable. Regenerate with [dune exec ocaml-tools/extract_bench/gen_fixtures.exe -- --write <dir>].

essential: The PDF body text says the east pier opens at six twelve
cases.note: A one-page PDF with a real xref table, written out by hand, the oracle's own fixture shape. The oracle's trafilatura backend reads it; this port refuses it by media type. The PDF decision lives in plans/seekwright-ocaml-port.md.

essential: Page one: the north pier keeps a ledger of every lamp

cases.note: Two pages, each with its own content stream.

essential: The kerned line is only readable when the pieces are joined
cases.note: Text set as a kerned TJ array, which separates a text extractor from a byte dumper.

The oracle's grinder: one large content stream referenced by every page, so parse work scales with the page count while the file stays far under the download cap. Any PDF backend added to this port has to answer inside fetch.timeout_seconds or refuse.
Cut in half: the objects are there, the xref table is not. The one outcome that is never defensible is success with no text.

essential: An xref stream document written without compression
cases.note: A PDF 1.5 document whose cross-reference is a stream object, the shape modern writers produce, written without a compression filter so the fixture tests structure rather than a decoder.
The oracle's own bytes for this case, NUL included.
